contributions.headingText: Squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) of the epididymis is a primary malignant epithelial neoplasm exhibiting squamous differentiation.
2C84 & XH0945 Malignant neoplasms of other specified male genital organs & Squamous cell carcinoma, NOS
Paratesticular SCC has been reported to arise from the epididymis and the tunica vaginalis lining chronic hydrocoele {2227843; 30596017}.

Patients present with a hard scrotal mass with or without hydrocoele [[Rowlands RP, Nicholson GW. A case of primary squamous-celled epithelioma of the epididymis. Lancet. 1909;173(4457):304–6. doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(00)44747-1.]] [[Artemyeva AS, Mamizhev EM, Nosov AK, et al. A rare case of squamous cell carcinoma of the paratesticular tissues. J Cancer Prev Curr Res. 2018 Mar 23;9(2):74–5. doi:10.15406/jcpcr.2018.09.00323.]].
To date, 4 cases have been reported: 2 in the epididymis and 2 in the tunica vaginalis. The patient age range is 27–85 years.

SCC is related to chronic inflammatory processes and subsequent squamous metaplasia. However, this relationship has not been evaluated because of the extremely low incidence of SCC {31019832; 20358011}.

Tumour size ranges from 45 to 110 mm [[Rowlands RP, Nicholson GW. A case of primary squamous-celled epithelioma of the epididymis. Lancet. 1909;173(4457):304–6. doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(00)44747-1.]] [[Artemyeva AS, Mamizhev EM, Nosov AK, et al. A rare case of squamous cell carcinoma of the paratesticular tissues. J Cancer Prev Curr Res. 2018 Mar 23;9(2):74–5. doi:10.15406/jcpcr.2018.09.00323.]] {2227843; 30596017}.

In 2 cases, the tumours were centred at the epididymis (1 of these involved the tunica vaginalis and testis). The remaining 2 cases originated from the tunica vaginalis lining the hydrocoele wall. The tumour appears grey-white and infiltrative, with areas of necrosis and haemorrhage [[Rowlands RP, Nicholson GW. A case of primary squamous-celled epithelioma of the epididymis. Lancet. 1909;173(4457):304–6. doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(00)44747-1.]] [[Artemyeva AS, Mamizhev EM, Nosov AK, et al. A rare case of squamous cell carcinoma of the paratesticular tissues. J Cancer Prev Curr Res. 2018 Mar 23;9(2):74–5. doi:10.15406/jcpcr.2018.09.00323.]].

The tumours display variably pleomorphic squamous cells, individual cells, keratinization, nuclear hyperchromasia, eosinophilic to amphophilic to clear cytoplasm, well-demarcated cell borders, and an absence of intercellular bridges. Mitotic figures, necrosis, and lymphovascular invasion may be identified {2227843; 30596017}.

The differential diagnosis includes a direct extension of a scrotal or skin adnexal primary SCC, teratoma with somatic-type malignancy, and SCC metastasis from extratesticular sites {30596017}.

Essential: malignant cytological features (nuclear atypia, enlargement, pleomorphism, hyperchromasia, loss of polarity, and overlapping) and architectural features (abnormal epithelial maturation) with squamous differentiation; exclusion of metastases and direct involvement from other sites.
There is no American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) staging system for this tumour.

In a well-documented case, a 46-year-old man with SCC of the epididymis developed ascites and died after 7 weeks [[Rowlands RP, Nicholson GW. A case of primary squamous-celled epithelioma of the epididymis. Lancet. 1909;173(4457):304–6. doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(00)44747-1.]]. The patient with epididymal squamous carcinoma with tunica vaginalis and testicular involvement developed lymph node and lung metastases and was treated with chemotherapy [[Rowlands RP, Nicholson GW. A case of primary squamous-celled epithelioma of the epididymis. Lancet. 1909;173(4457):304–6. doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(00)44747-1.]] [[Artemyeva AS, Mamizhev EM, Nosov AK, et al. A rare case of squamous cell carcinoma of the paratesticular tissues. J Cancer Prev Curr Res. 2018 Mar 23;9(2):74–5. doi:10.15406/jcpcr.2018.09.00323.]]. One of the two patients with SCC arising in the tunica vaginalis received adjuvant radiation and chemotherapy but developed inguinal lymph node metastasis 2 months after the initial diagnosis {30596017}.
